item.body_evidence_excerpt: Most parts of Sarawak will be experiencing hot weather and reduced rainfall until August 14, said Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip. In addition, southern Sarawak is set to experience transboundary haze due to increased hotspots in the neighbouring country, he said. “Analysis of the latest weather forecast models indicate that hot weather and below-average rainfall are expected in most parts of Borneo, including Sarawak, until August 14. “The influence of southerly winds, combined with the anticipated high number of hot spots in the neighbouring country, could lead to transboundary haze and reduced visibility, particularly in southern Sarawak,” he said in a notice. There are now eight locations in Sarawak where the monitoring stations recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings. — The Borneo Post

item.body_evidence_excerpt: The Health Ministry (MOH) is strengthening surveillance of haze-related illnesses at health facilities following 10 stations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, with nine in Sarawak and one in Selangor. In a statement today, MOH said the preparedness of health facilities, medicine supplies and healthcare personnel had also been stepped up to ensure health services could be provided appropriately should there be an increase in haze-related cases. According to the ministry, based on the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) at 9 am yesterday, the nine areas in Sarawak recording unhealthy API readings were Serian, Samarahan, Kuching, Bintulu, Samalaju, Mukah, Sibu, Sarikei and Sri Aman, while the other area was Johan Setia in Selangor. MOH advised the public, particularly those in affected areas, to reduce physical and strenuous outdoor activities when the API exceeds 100 and to wear an appropriate face mask if they needed to be outdoors. State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) chairman Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas said the mitigation measure was aimed at addressing prolonged hot and dry weather conditions that could affect water supply sources and worsen haze in several areas. “The main focus of OPA Series 3 will be on identified critical dam and water catchment areas, particularly those important for ensuring the continuity of water supply and maintaining dam levels. “The implementation is subject to the availability of suitable clouds, atmospheric conditions and favourable meteorological factors,” he said in a statement today.
